question.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}{z}^{2}\,\text{d}S
$$

where $S$ is defined by $z={e}^{x}$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $x\le y\le x+1.$
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=g(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f(x,y,z)$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

For the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂x}=\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x})={e}^{x},
$$

and

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂y}=\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x})=0.
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be evaluated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}{z}^{2}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,{z}^{2}\sqrt{1+{e}^{2x}+{0}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,{e}^{2x}\sqrt{1+{e}^{2x}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{x+1}{e}^{2x}\sqrt{1+{e}^{2x}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[{e}^{2x}\sqrt{1+{e}^{2x}}y]}_{y=x}^{y=x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{2x}\sqrt{1+{e}^{2x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{3}(1+{e}^{2x})^{3/2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}((1+{e}^{2})^{3/2}-{2}^{3/2})\end{aligned}
$$
